tldr_label: TL;DR — The Fed holds in a split vote; Microsoft rises while Alphabet falls; Spain mourns 68 dead in a rail crash

tldr_bullets.label: Fed
tldr_bullets.body: The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with two members dissenting in favor of a hike. Chair Warsh said politics played 'no role' in the decision. [[TAG:info:10-2 hold]]

tldr_bullets.label: Big Tech
tldr_bullets.body: After hours, Microsoft rose on a beat while Alphabet fell about 9%, CNBC reported. In Seoul, Samsung slid despite record profit and the Kospi fell back below 6,000.

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: With about 93% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's bloc had 53 seats, Eisenkot's 48 and Arab parties 19. Herzog will begin coalition consultations after certification. [[TAG:warning:no majority]]

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: The WSJ reported that Vance wrote to Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei to revive peace talks. Accounts differ on what Trump authorized.

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: Officials said a Russian jet-powered drone hit a train at Dnipro station and killed 13. The Kremlin said Europe will not be at the next talks in Abu Dhabi. [[TAG:danger:13 killed]]

tldr_bullets.label: Spain
tldr_bullets.body: At least 68 people died when a high-speed train hit a stopped train near Toledo. Sánchez declared three days of national mourning. [[TAG:danger:68 dead]]

sections.title: Fed Holds, Split Vote
sections.summary: Rates stay at 3.75% to 4.00% as two officials dissent in favor of a hike; the ECB decides today

paragraphs.heading: The decision
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that the Fed held its target range at 3.75% to 4.00% in a 10-2 vote. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack wanted a quarter-point increase. Bloomberg said the statement cited the need for more data and gave no clear signal on a December hike. Yahoo Finance reported that Chair Kevin Warsh said politics played 'no role' in the decision days before the midterms. [[TAG:info:2 hawkish dissents]]

paragraphs.heading: Market close
paragraphs.body: The Motley Fool reported that the S&P 500 rose 0.28% to 7,743.98, and StockTitan reported that the Dow added 0.19% to 52,475.10. The Nasdaq rose about 0.27%. After the bell, Fortinet dropped sharply.

paragraphs.heading: ECB today
paragraphs.body: FXStreet and TioMarkets expect the ECB to hold its deposit rate at 2.50% today, with the focus on whether President Lagarde signals a December hike. The decision is due at 14:15 CET.

sections.title: Earnings Split
sections.summary: Investors reward Microsoft and punish Alphabet; Samsung slides despite record profit

paragraphs.heading: Microsoft and Alphabet
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported adjusted EPS of $4.89 for Microsoft against roughly $4.73 expected, and revenue of $92.28 billion against $90.69 billion expected, driven by Azure. Estimates of the after-hours gain vary: CNBC said about 2% and StockTitan 4.9%. CNBC said Alphabet fell about 9% in extended trading. Yahoo Finance framed the night as a test of whether the AI boom is paying off. [[TAG:warning:Alphabet -9%]]

paragraphs.heading: Samsung and Seoul
paragraphs.body: SBS reported that Samsung's third-quarter operating profit hit a record of about 107 trillion won. CNBC said the shares closed 4.13% lower because the result fell just short of estimates and investors had hoped for larger shareholder returns. The Korea Times reported that the Kospi was down about 3% in late morning trading, and IBTimes said it slipped back below 6,000 after the previous day's rally.

sections.title: Israel After the Vote
sections.summary: Netanyahu's bloc edges ahead at 53 seats as Herzog prepares consultations after certification

paragraphs.heading: Near-final count
paragraphs.body: Ynet and the Jerusalem Post reported that, with nearly all votes counted, Netanyahu's bloc had 53 seats, Eisenkot's 48 and the Arab parties 19, with Likud at 26 and Yashar at 21. Bloomberg said Netanyahu overtook Eisenkot after early counts had shown the opposition ahead. Double-envelope ballots could still shift the totals. [[TAG:warning:not certified]]

paragraphs.heading: Next steps
paragraphs.body: ABC News (Australia) reported that President Herzog urged party leaders to come to consultations with an 'open mind'. Those talks will begin once the final results are presented. Eisenkot's path to a majority runs through the Arab parties, but allies Avigdor Liberman and Naftali Bennett have ruled out relying on them. The nominee will have up to six weeks to form a government.

sections.title: Iran and the Gulf
sections.summary: Vance reaches out to Tehran as Houthi missiles keep targeting Saudi Arabia; Brent tops $114

paragraphs.heading: Vance letter
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel and Iran International, citing the Wall Street Journal, reported that Vice President JD Vance wrote to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, to try to restart peace talks. Accounts of Trump's role differ: The Week reported that he denied ordering negotiations and said the letter concerned medical supplies, while MEAWW reported that he approved the contact. No resumed talks have been confirmed. [[TAG:warning:accounts differ]]

paragraphs.heading: Oil and the Houthis
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Brent rose 1.3% on Wednesday to settle at $115.32, while HDFC Sky said prices eased on Thursday on hopes of talks after the Vance reports. TBS News reported that the Saudi-led coalition intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile fired toward the Eastern Province, the latest in a month of attacks on the kingdom.

sections.title: Ukraine and Russia
sections.summary: Drone strike on a Dnipro train kills 13; Kremlin shuts Europe out of Abu Dhabi talks

paragraphs.heading: Dnipro strike
paragraphs.body: The Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post reported that a Russian jet-powered drone hit a train at Dnipro station that was preparing to leave for Zaporizhzhia. Governor Oleksandr Hanzha said 13 people were killed and at least five injured. Ukrainian Railways said people stayed on the platform despite an air raid alert. [[TAG:danger:13 killed]]

paragraphs.heading: Talks without Europe
paragraphs.body: Kyiv Post reported that Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said European countries will not be invited to the next Russia-US-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, which could take place after November 4. Finnish President Stubb had said Europe would be involved. The Kyiv Independent reported that Moscow says the 'battlefield situation' will decide the timing.

paragraphs.heading: Moscow courts Africa
paragraphs.body: AP, via the Washington Times, reported that Putin opened the third Russia-Africa summit in Moscow and pitched Russia as a better partner than the West. CNBC Africa said he described the West as 'colonial'.

sections.title: Europe
sections.summary: High-speed crash near Toledo kills 68; EU and Canada open talks on an alliance

paragraphs.heading: Toledo crash
paragraphs.body: CBS News and CNN reported that at least 68 people were killed when a RENFE high-speed train hit the back of a stopped Iryo train near Urda, south of Madrid. Officials said 58 people were in hospital. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declared three days of national mourning and promised firm action if negligence is found. The cause is unknown. It is Spain's second deadly high-speed collision this year. [[TAG:danger:68 dead]]

paragraphs.heading: EU-Canada summit
paragraphs.body: Carney hosts António Costa and Ursula von der Leyen in Montreal on October 29 and 30 to launch formal talks on a deeper partnership, BNN Bloomberg reported. The Boston Globe said an 'associate member' label proposed for Canada faces resistance from France and Germany.
